function: Channel estimation for time-varying frequency-selective uplink MIMO-OFDM: BPCM-based LMMSE gives coarse estimates, then a 3D dilated residual CNN denoises and interpolates over time, frequency, and antennas. p. 1
system: Uplink multiuser MIMO-OFDM, BS with M=64 antennas, K=24 single-antenna users, N=48 subcarriers at 30 kHz spacing, T=28 symbols (8 pilots); no RIS; carrier frequency not stated. p. 4
method: LMMSE on a block-wise planar channel model followed by a 3D dilated residual CNN (3D-DRCN); supervised offline training with L1 loss and Adam, learning rate 1e-4. p. 4
data_channel: 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL-B simulated channels; training with 100-300 ns delay spread, 80-120 km/h, SNR 4-14 dB; testing with 129 ns, 100 km/h, SNR 4-18 dB. p. 4
test_conditions: Test on CDL-B with 129 ns and 100 km/h, inside the training ranges (100-300 ns, 80-120 km/h); test SNR 4-18 dB, training 4-14 dB. p. 4
baselines: Learned: CE-DNN, CE-CNN, SF-CNN, Model2, ICINet, LDAMP, LTMP, 2DU, 3DFF. Classical: LS, 1D LMMSE, 2x1D LMMSE; ablation: Module A without the network. p. 4
metrics: NMSE versus SNR; number of complex multiplications versus number of users. p. 4
complexity: Counts complex multiplications: module A, (NT/VU)^3+6K(NTP/VU)^2+3KUVM(NTP/VU); module B, (12170+30T)TP*N*M*K/4; over one order below LDAMP, nearly three below LTMP. p. 4-5
q1_support: p. 4: "we use the CDL-B channel model [16]" for training and testing; reference [16] on p. 5 is 3GPP TR 38.901.
q2_support: p. 4: "For testing, we use the CDL-B channel with 129 ns r.m.s. delay spread and mobile speed of 100 km/h"; both lie inside the training ranges, and only the SNR extends beyond (4-18 dB versus 4-14 dB), which is an SNR sweep. No other scenario, array size or user number is tested.
q3_support: p. 4: "ICINet [11], LDAMP [13], LTMP [14], 2DU [18], 3DFF [18], LS, 2 × 1D LMMSE, 1D LMMSE" are the learned and non-learned baselines, compared on NMSE (p. 4: "Fig. 5 shows the channel estimation MSE against SNR").
q4_support: p. 4: "the complex multiplications number is (12170 + 30T )TP NMK /4"; p. 5: "the computational complexity of LBPCE is reduced by more than one order of magnitude compared with LDAMP".
q5_support: p. 4: "For the network training, we use the CDL-B channel model [16]"; channels are generated from a 3GPP model, not a public dataset or measured data, and the letter gives no code or data link.
notes: Included, area 2: the learned 3D-DRCN refines the channel estimates, while module A is classical LMMSE. CDL-B comes from 3GPP TR 38.901 (reference [16], p. 5). Test delay spread and speed fall inside the training ranges, so q2 is 0. The title and DOI on p. 1 match the work.
